question: PQRS is a trapezium in which QR || PS and PR = RS. If ∠PQR = 96° and ∠QPR = 34°, then what is the measure of ∠PRS?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In **ΔPQR**, sum of angles = 180° ⇒ ∠PRQ = 180° − (96° + 34°) = 50°.

Since **QR || PS**, alternate interior angles are equal ⇒ ∠SPR = ∠PRQ = 50°.

In **ΔPRS**, given **PR = RS**, so angles opposite to equal sides are equal ⇒ ∠PSR = ∠SPR = 50°.

Sum of angles in **ΔPRS** = 180° ⇒ ∠PRS = 180° − (50° + 50°) = 80°.

**∴ The correct answer is 80°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **PQRS** is a **trapezium** with **QR || PS**. **PR = RS**, **∠PQR = 96°**, and **∠QPR = 34°**.

**Formula Used:** Angle sum property of a triangle (Sum = 180°) and alternate interior angles property (when two lines are parallel).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a89828ee123eb6136adc0d44e4ba7f7bf51c311c969b827c292d2daadeace964.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ In **ΔPQR**, ∠PQR + ∠QPR + ∠PRQ = 180°

⇒ 96° + 34° + ∠PRQ = 180°

⇒ 130° + ∠PRQ = 180°

⇒ ∠PRQ = 50°

⇒ Since **QR || PS**, ∠SPR = ∠PRQ (**Alternate Interior Angles**)

⇒ ∠SPR = 50°

⇒ In **ΔPRS**, given **PR = RS**, therefore ∠PSR = ∠SPR = 50° (Angles opposite to equal sides)

⇒ ∠PRS + ∠PSR + ∠SPR = 180°

⇒ ∠PRS + 50° + 50° = 180°

⇒ ∠PRS + 100° = 180°

⇒ ∠PRS = 80°

**∴ The correct answer is 80°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Isosceles Triangle Property

In a triangle, if two sides are equal, the angles opposite to those sides are also equal.

Parallel Lines & Transversals

When a transversal intersects two parallel lines, the **alternate interior angles** are always equal.

Angle Sum Property

The sum of all interior angles of any triangle is always 180°.</p
